title: Female body: anterior anatomy
description: A glass-body view of the female: major organs in place, with breasts, uterus and ovaries completing the picture.

questions.question: Where are the main organs in the female body?
questions.answer: The brain lies in the skull; lungs and heart in the chest; digestive and urinary organs in the abdomen; and uterus, tubes and ovaries in the pelvis.

questions.question: Does a female body map show every deep structure?
questions.answer: No. It is a regional orientation view. Detailed chapters explain deeper pelvic supports, breast tissue, nerves and microscopic layers that a single image cannot resolve.

questions.question: Where is the brain shown on the female body map?
questions.answer: Control centre housed in the skull, glowing through the translucent scalp. Function: Integrates sensation, movement, thought, memory and autonomic drive.

questions.question: Where are the lungs in the female body map?
questions.answer: Paired thoracic organs flanking the heart. Function: Gas exchange across ~300 million alveoli.

questions.question: What does the liver do in the female body?
questions.answer: Function: Metabolism, detoxification, bile, plasma proteins. Largest internal organ, right upper quadrant.
